lots.working: No same-item SOLD in similar condition: the only 201 sale ($110 hammer) came with case base, manual and accessories, which lot 1491 lacks. Under the rules keep_max = 0 and flip_max = 0. For reference only: $110/1.198 = $91.8, so if the user treats the 201K as same-item the ceiling would be $90 hammer, and a bare 201P should sit below that (my judgement, roughly $40 to $70 hammer). lots.question_for_gowans: Does lot 1491 run (motor and light) on test, are the cords and foot control sound, is the bobbin case and bobbin present, and is there a base, case or lid with it?

For reference only: if the Woodfast were treated as same-item, $850/1.198 = $709.5, rounded $705, which I think is too generous for an unbadged, untested machine; on the photos a cautious buyer would want it well under $400 hammer unless it is a known European brand and runs.

lots.guide_summary: All SOLD at Gowans (Feb to Sep 2026), no UNSOLD or ASKING evidence. Sound all-metal 9ct rings of 5.4g to 7.6g hammered $310 to $460, which is $55 to $69 per gram; scaled to 5.1g that is about $280 to $350 hammer. The closest match, a 7.6g engraved signet, made $450 on 27 Sep 2026 ($59/g, about $302 at 5.1g). All AUD, rate 1. Melt (floor, not a sale): XAU USD 4103.40 (api.gold-api.com, 2026-10-07) x 1.43284 AUD per USD (open.er-api.com, 2026-10-07) / 31.1035 = AUD 189.0/g pure; x 0.375 = AUD 70.9/g; x 5.1g = about AUD 361.
lots.working: Keep: no identical 5.1g signet sold, so I weight-adjust the sound all-metal SOLD entries. Lowest per-gram rate = $330/6g = $55/g (lot 398081, Mar 2026). 5.1g x $55 = $280.50 hammer equivalent. $280.50 / 1.198 = $234.1, rounded down to $230 hammer (all-in about $275.54, about 76% of melt). Flip: likely resale about $300 (Gowans sound-ring level of $57 to $59/g x 5.1g, or about 83% of the $361 melt from a scrap buyer), less 10% selling fee ($30), no outbound postage (local sale) = $270; $270 / 2.396 = $112.7, rounded down to $110 hammer.
lots.confidence_reason: The 9ct Rodd stamp was read in the photo, and at least five sound 9ct all-metal ring sales within 12 months were checked in the API, with photos viewed. Weight is Gowans' figure, not verified.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped lot 402968 ($150, 9ct ring 5.1g size X): same weight and size but its photo shows a stone-set ring (square brown cabochon), so the gram figure includes the stone; not the same item. Dropped lot 363330 ($83, broken Rodd signet with stone missing), lot 416044 ($145, unmarked part signet) and lot 422431 ($160, 9ct part ring 5g): damaged or part pieces, not comparable condition (they show the scrap downside of about $30/g). Corrected the researcher's price-string slips: lot 363352 is $120, not $125; lot 382225 is $400, the '$330' text was spurious.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: yellow gold signet with a shaped shield head engraved with a script monogram (looks like 'JRD' or similar), shoulders with scroll detail, shank looks fairly slim. Photo 2 (enlarged): stamp under the head reads '9ct' (worn) over 'Rodd'. Surface scratches and wear on the head; no visible cracks or solder seams in the two photos, but the back of the shank is not fully shown.
lots.condition: Worn, scratched, engraving softened; shank looks slim but intact in the photos. Weight 5.1g and size X per Gowans.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please confirm lot 9 weighs 5.1g on your scale, and check that the shank is not cracked, very thin or repaired at the back.
